must_fix.title: Dialog ignores autoFocus and loses focus on close when a child has autoFocus
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx:59 captures document.activeElement in a passive useEffect, after React has focused the autoFocus child, and :86 focusFirst() then overrides it. Probe: trigger opens a Dialog containing <button>First</button><input autoFocus/>, then Escape is pressed. Output: 'P1 focused after open: <button>First</button>' and 'P1 focused after close: <body>...'. The autoFocus input never gets focus, and focus is not returned to the trigger.

must_fix.title: Nested dialogs opened in the same render trap focus in the outer dialog
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx:61-70: effects run child-first, so the inner dialog's token is pushed before the outer's and the outer counts as topmost. Probe: outer and inner Dialog both rendered with open at mount, then focus moved to 'Inner btn 2'. Output: 'P2 initial focus: Outer btn' and 'P2 after focusing inner btn 2: Outer btn'. The visible top dialog cannot take focus.

report:
I wouldn't merge this yet. `pnpm test` passes (75 tests in 3 files) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean, but I confirmed three behaviour bugs with a probe test. I put that probe at `src/zz_probe.test.tsx`, deleted it afterwards, and `git status` is back to exactly how I found it. ### Must fix 1. **Dialog ignores `autoFocus` and loses focus when it closes** (`src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx:59` and `:86`). The dialog records the element that had focus before opening in a `useEffect`. That runs after React has already focused any `autoFocus` child, so it records the element inside the dialog. Then `focusFirst()` moves focus anyway. Probe: a trigger button opens a dialog containing ``, then Escape is pressed. ``` P1 focused after open: P1 focused after close: ... ``` The `autoFocus` input never gets focus. On close, focus goes to `` instead of the trigger, which breaks "returns focus to whatever had it before opening". The fix is to capture the previous focus before the commit and to respect an `autoFocus` element if one is present. 2. **Nested dialogs that open in the same render trap focus in the wrong dialog** (`Dialog.tsx:61-70`). Effects run child-first, so the inner dialog pushes its entry onto `openDialogs` before the outer one. The outer dialog then counts as topmost. Probe: an outer and inner dialog both rendered with `open`, then focus is moved to "Inner btn 2". ``` P2 initial focus: Outer btn P2 after focusing inner btn 2: Outer btn ``` The visible top dialog can't receive focus at all. The existing nested test only covers opening the inner dialog after the outer one. 3. **Combobox gives no visible sign of the active option** (`src/Combobox/Combobox.tsx:145-160`). The active option is only referenced from `aria-activedescendant` on the input. The `
  • ` carries no attribute for it, and CSS can't select an element through an id reference, so a consumer can't style it. After two ArrowDowns the listbox renders as: ```
